lines: The trip made the village feel larger and home feel more exact.
I learned which roads look safe from here and which ones only pretend.
Next time, I pack lighter, listen faster, and trust the quiet <pulse>less</pulse>.
It is strange how far a road can stretch once you are actually walking it.
I saw enough out there to respect every map a little more.
Some paths look simple until your feet are the ones proving them wrong.
I came back with tired legs and better questions.
The world feels different when the village is behind you instead of around you.
I learned that distance has a way of making small worries feel large.
Next time we travel, I will know what to watch for before it starts watching us.
Going out there reminded me why doors matter.
I brought back more than sore feet. I brought back a sharper idea of <pulse>home</pulse>.
A village looks different after you have had to find your way back to it.
The road has its lessons, but I am glad ours led back here.
I missed the sound of familiar work more than I expected.
Home feels smaller after travel, but not weaker.
I understand the village better now that I have seen what waits beyond it.
There is comfort in knowing which door is yours before night falls.
The world outside is wide. That makes a warm hearth feel wiser.
I came back tired, but more certain of where I belong.
